approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: Park at the Eagle Creek/Oval trailhead (~3,000 ft) at the end of FR 4420-080, reached via Twisp River Road/FR 44 (~12.5 mi west of Twisp) and the West Buttermilk/FR 4420 spur.

pins.name: Eagle Creek/Oval Trailhead
pins.note: Self-issue Northwest Forest Pass / $5 day-use fee at the kiosk; trail enters Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness a short way in, vault toilet and stock ramp at the lot.
pins.directions: Park at the Eagle Creek/Oval trailhead at about 3,000 ft, at the end of FR 4420-080. Reach it on Twisp River Road/FR 44 roughly 12.5 miles west of Twisp, then turn up the West Buttermilk/FR 4420 spur and follow it to the road's end. There is a vault toilet and a stock ramp at the lot; self-issue a Northwest Forest Pass or pay the $5 day-use fee at the kiosk, and the trail enters the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness a short way in. The access road and the lake basins are typically snow-free from early July into October.

pins.name: Eagle Creek / Oval Creek Trail junction
pins.note: Ford the side stream here, then turn left off Eagle Creek Trail #410 onto Oval Creek Trail #410A toward the Oval Lakes basin.

pins.name: Oval Creek / Oval Lakes Trail junction
pins.note: Bear onto Oval Lakes Trail #410B, which climbs past an old moraine below Gray Peak before dropping into the Oval Lakes basin — this section burned in the 2018 Crescent Fire and is dry/dusty with little shade.

pins.name: Middle Oval Lake outflow
pins.note: Maintained trail ends at the lake outflow; established stock/backpacker camp with fishing (cutthroat) — this is where you leave the trail and start up open heather/talus toward the Sawtooth crest.

pins.name: Saddle on Oval Peak's south ridge
pins.note: Gain the Sawtooth crest via open heather and talus above the lake's outflow; no maintained tread here, easy to lose the line in fog or low visibility.

pins.name: Talus/boulder field on the south ridge crest
pins.note: Broad ridge of loose, sometimes slick talus and large boulders — the crux annoyance of the route (twisted-ankle terrain, not technical).

pins.name: Oval Peak
pins.note: Highest point in the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness and of the Methow Mountains; small rock glacier on the north slopes, views of Star, Courtney, and Gray Peaks.
